classification.difficultyReason: Combines adjacency, alternating positions, grouped elements and gap counting.

content.prompt: Bob, Mary, Charlie, Jane, David and Emily go to the cinema and decide to sit together in the same row. Find the number of different seating arrangements if

answer.worked:
Arrange the six distinct people in a line.

$$N=6!=720.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Bob wishes to sit on an end.

answer.worked:
Bob has two choices of end. Arrange the other five people in the remaining seats.

$$\begin{align*}N&=2\times5!\\N&=240\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: the men and women are to alternate.

answer.worked:
There are two alternating patterns: men first or women first. Arrange Bob, Charlie and David in the three men's positions, and Mary, Jane and Emily in the three women's positions.

$$\begin{align*}N&=2\times3!\times3!\\N&=72\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Bob and Mary wish to sit together.

answer.worked:
Treat Bob and Mary as one block, giving five elements to arrange. Their order within the block has two choices.

$$\begin{align*}N&=2!\times5!\\N&=240\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Bob and Mary wish to sit together, and the men and women are to alternate.

answer.short:
$2\times5\times2!\times2!=40$

Use the two alternating patterns and five possible adjacent seat pairs.
answer.worked:
Choose one of the two alternating patterns. Bob and Mary can occupy any of the five adjacent seat pairs, with their order fixed by the pattern. Arrange the remaining two men and two women in their positions.

$$\begin{align*}N&=2\times5\times2!\times2!\\N&=40\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: Charlie and Jane will not sit next to each other.

answer.short:
$4!\times5\times4=480$

Place Charlie and Jane in different gaps around the other four people.
answer.worked:
Arrange the other four people in $4!$ ways. They create five gaps, including the ends. Charlie has five gap choices and Jane has four different gap choices.

$$\begin{align*}N&=4!\times5\times4\\N&=480\end{align*}$$

children.label: g
children.prompt: David and Emily are to sit together, and Bob and Mary are to sit together.

answer.short:
$2\times2\times4!=96$

Treat each specified pair as a block.
answer.worked:
Treat David and Emily as one block and Bob and Mary as another. Arrange these two blocks, Charlie and Jane in $4!$ ways. Each block has two internal orders.

$$\begin{align*}N&=2!\times2!\times4!\\N&=96\end{align*}$$

children.label: h
children.prompt: Mary is to sit immediately between Bob and Jane.

answer.short:
$2\times4!=48$

Treat Bob–Mary–Jane or Jane–Mary–Bob as one block.
answer.worked:
The three-person block has two orders: Bob–Mary–Jane or Jane–Mary–Bob. Arrange this block with Charlie, David and Emily as four elements.

$$\begin{align*}N&=2\times4!\\N&=48\end{align*}$$

children.label: i
children.prompt: David and Mary are to sit together, and Charlie and Emily are not to sit together.

answer.short:
$2\times3!\times4\times3=144$

Group David and Mary, then place Charlie and Emily in different gaps.
answer.worked:
Treat David and Mary as a block with two internal orders. Arrange the block, Bob and Jane in $3!$ ways. These three elements create four gaps. Charlie has four gap choices and Emily has three different gap choices.

$$\begin{align*}N&=2\times3!\times4\times3\\N&=144\end{align*}$$
